abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achaia.title: Achaia
achaia.note: The Roman province covering southern Greece, with Corinth in it, where Paul spent a long stretch and wrote back afterwards.

amplias.title: Amplias
amplias.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
amplias.note: Paul greets him in the closing list of Romans as "my beloved in the Lord." The fuller form, Ampliatus, was common among slaves and freedmen, and a decorated early Christian tomb in the Catacomb of Domitilla bears it, though nobody can prove it is the same man.

andronicus.title: Andronicus
andronicus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
andronicus.note: Paul greets Andronicus, a Jewish Christian and his relative or countryman, together with Junia in Romans 16:7. He calls the pair outstanding among the apostles and says they believed in Christ before he did.

apelles.title: Apelles
apelles.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
apelles.note: Paul calls him "approved in Christ," which suggests faith that had been tested. Nothing else is known about him.

aquila.title: Aquila
aquila.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aquila.note: A Jewish tentmaker from Pontus. He and his wife Priscilla had been expelled from Rome with other Jews, met Paul in Corinth, and worked beside him. Churches met in their home in more than one city.

aristobulus.title: Aristobulus
aristobulus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
aristobulus.note: Paul greets his household and not the man himself, who may have died or may not have believed. Some think he was a grandson of Herod the Great known from Josephus to have lived in Rome, but that cannot be confirmed.

asia.title: Asia
asia.note: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.

asyncritos.title: Asyncritos
asyncritos.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
asyncritos.note: Greeted by Paul with Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes and others in Rome. Beyond his name and that group nothing is known.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

cencrea.title: Cencrea
cencrea.note: Corinth's eastern harbour on the Saronic Gulf, about seven miles from the city. Paul cut his hair there for a vow before he sailed, and the town had a church of its own.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

elijah.title: Elijah
elijah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elijah.note: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who took on Ahab and Jezebel over Baal worship and beat 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel with fire from heaven. Straight after, he ran into the wilderness sure he was the last faithful man left, and God met him in a quiet voice, not in wind or earthquake or fire. He did not die; a whirlwind took him up while Elisha watched.

epenetus.title: Epenetus
epenetus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
epenetus.note: Paul greets him in Rome as beloved, the first convert to Christ from the province of Asia.

erastus.title: Erastus
erastus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
erastus.note: Paul's companion, and in Romans the city treasurer of Corinth. An inscription found at Corinth names an Erastus who paid for a pavement in return for an aedileship.

gaius.title: Gaius
gaius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
gaius.note: This Gaius was Paul's host when Romans was written, and one of the few Paul baptised himself in Corinth. The name was common, and at least three men carry it across Paul's circle, so which references belong to the same man is hard to say.

hermas.title: Hermas
hermas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
hermas.note: A Roman Christian Paul greets in his letter. Later tradition sometimes made him the author of The Shepherd of Hermas, but that book is almost certainly another man's, written a generation or more later.

hermes-2.title: Hermes
hermes-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
hermes-2.note: Paul greets him at the end of Romans, among a list of believers in Rome. He shares a name with the Greek messenger god, and that is all anyone knows.

herodion.title: Herodion
herodion.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
herodion.note: He gets a greeting from Paul in Rome, who calls him "kinsman", most likely meaning a fellow Jew. The name comes from the Herod family, so he may have belonged to a Herodian household.

illyricum.title: Illyricum
illyricum.note: Paul says he preached as far as Illyricum, and that was the farthest he went. It lay along the eastern Adriatic, roughly modern Albania and the Dalmatian coast.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

israelite.title: Israelite
israelite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israelite.note: One of the people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel. Paul calls himself an Israelite in Romans 11 when he argues God has not dropped his people.

jacob-2.title: Jacob
jacob-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob-2.note: In the New Testament the name mostly means the patriarch, set beside Abraham and Isaac, and Luke's angel promises Mary that Jesus will reign "over the house of Jacob forever". Matthew's genealogy also has a Jacob as the father of Joseph.

jason.title: Jason
jason.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jason.note: Paul and Silas stayed with him in Thessalonica. When a mob came for Paul and could not find him, they dragged Jason before the city officials instead, charging him with harbouring men who defied Caesar's decrees, and he had to post bond to go free.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

julia.title: Julia
julia.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
julia.note: Paul greets her at the end of Romans, alongside Philologus, Nereus and his sister. The name was common in Rome and may tie her to a household of the Julian family, as a freedwoman or slave. Nothing else about her is recorded.

junias.title: Junias
junias.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
junias.note: Paul calls Andronicus and Junias his relatives and fellow prisoners, "outstanding among the apostles." Whether the name is the masculine Junias or the much more common feminine Junia is argued, and most modern scholars now read Junia, a woman.

lucius.title: Lucius
lucius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
lucius.note: One of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, from Cyrene, there when the Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul apart. Paul sends greetings from a Lucius he calls his kinsman in Romans 16:21, and whether that is the same man is uncertain.

macedonia.title: Macedonia
macedonia.note: The Roman province over northern Greece. Paul crossed into it after a vision of a man pleading, "Come over into Macedonia and help us," and went on through Philippi, Thessalonica and Berea, where Christian mission in Europe is usually said to begin. He came back at least twice and praised its churches for giving out of their poverty.

narcissus.title: Narcissus
narcissus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
narcissus.note: Paul greets the believers in the household of Narcissus, not the man himself. Some guess he was a rich freedman tied to the emperor's court; the text does not say.

nereus.title: Nereus
nereus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
nereus.note: Paul greets him and his sister in Rome at the end of the letter to the Romans, and nothing else is known.

olympas.title: Olympas
olympas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
olympas.note: Paul greets him by name at the end of Romans, a Christian in Rome about whom nothing more is known.

patrobas.title: Patrobas
patrobas.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
patrobas.note: He is greeted in Rome along with Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes and Hermas. Nothing further about him is recorded.

persis.title: Persis
persis.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
persis.note: Paul calls her "beloved" and says she "labored much in the Lord." She was a Christian woman at Rome, greeted in Romans 16:12, and Paul uses that kind of language for real work in ministry.

phebe.title: Phebe
phebe.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
phebe.note: A servant of the church at Cenchreae, the eastern port of Corinth, whom Paul commends to the Romans and who probably carried the letter to them herself.

philologus.title: Philologus
philologus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
philologus.note: Greeted at the end of Romans along with Julia, Nereus and others, probably all one household or house church.

phlegon.title: Phlegon
phlegon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
phlegon.note: Another of the names Paul greets in Rome, grouped with Asyncritus, Hermas, Patrobas and Hermes (Romans 16:14).

prisca.title: Prisca
prisca.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
prisca.note: Paul's formal Latin form of Priscilla, used in his letters.

quartus.title: Quartus
quartus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
quartus.note: A Christian at Corinth who joins in Paul's greetings at the end of Romans, mentioned beside Erastus, the city treasurer.

rufus-2.title: Rufus
rufus-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
rufus-2.note: Son of Simon of Cyrene, the man made to carry the cross. Mark names him as someone his readers would know.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

sion.title: Sion
sion.note: Another spelling of Zion. The hill in Jerusalem came to stand for the whole city, and in poetry for the place where God lives among his people.

sosipater.title: Sosipater
sosipater.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
sosipater.note: Paul's kinsman, who sent his greetings to the church at Rome along with Paul's. He is probably Sopater of Berea.

spain.title: Spain
spain.note: Paul meant to go on to Spain from Rome, once he had taken the collection to the poor in Jerusalem, and he hoped the Roman church would help him on his way. Whether he ever got there is not known.

stachys.title: Stachys
stachys.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
stachys.note: "My beloved," Paul calls him, in his long list of greetings to believers at Rome. Nothing more about him is recorded in the New Testament.

tertius.title: Tertius
tertius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
tertius.note: Paul dictated Romans and Tertius wrote it down. At the end he slips in a greeting of his own, in his own voice.

timotheus.title: Timotheus
timotheus.note: Timothy, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. Paul took him along on his travels and trusted him with hard errands to churches in trouble, and two of Paul's letters are addressed to him.

tryphena.title: Tryphena
tryphena.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
tryphena.note: She and Tryphosa are greeted by Paul at Rome as women who labored in the Lord. The names are so alike that some guess they were sisters, though the text does not say.

tryphosa.title: Tryphosa
tryphosa.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
tryphosa.note: Paul greets her at Rome with Tryphena, two women who worked hard in the Lord. The paired names may mean they were sisters. Nothing more is known of her.

urbanus.title: Urbanus
urbanus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
urbanus.note: A fellow worker Paul greets in Romans 16:9 along with Stachys. The King James spells him Urbane.
